_comment: PROMOTION REGISTRY for harness/tests/'s fast tier (round 385, harness A). Read by harness/tierbudget.py, which harness/tests/conftest.py consults when it applies the `swe_slow` marker. Round 235's filename rule still decides the DEFAULT and still decides it alone: a `test_swe_*.py` file ABSENT from `promoted` is slow, so a new file tiers itself with no edit here -- round 235's self-maintenance property, kept. This file can only ever move a file toward the tier a human is watching, and only on a measurement. A stale entry costs wall-clock; it cannot cost coverage. Two bars for an entry: MEASURED under `cap_s` by `tierbudget.py measure` (each file alone, fresh process, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1), and GREEN when measured -- a red file is never promotable however cheap, because the fast tier is what the driver's per-round health check reports and a promotion must not turn every future round's line red for a defect it did not cause. Every promoted file is re-timed FOR FREE by the fast-tier run itself (conftest.py's pytest_terminal_summary hook), which prints a `tier-budget:` line above pytest's count line and says DRIFT when a file outgrows max(measured_s * drift_factor, measured_s + drift_floor_s). Do not hand-edit a `measured_s`: re-run the ladder and re-decide.

test_swe_coverage.py.why: coverage instrumentation over the whence tree; round 217 measured it with test_swe_triage.py at 150.4s for the pair, which is 28x its cost today

test_swe_mutation.py.why: the most expensive promotion and the one most likely to drift; kept because the cap is the policy and an unmeasured exemption is the thing this round removed

test_swe_oracles.py.why: holds all three injected-bug tests (fast_slow / direct / frames) — round 383 item 5's actual ask; these are the tests that go red on a language change and the whole reason the tier was re-measured

test_swe_prioritize.py.why: was NEVER measured (`unknown` in the slow-tier ledger) and was 60% red on this host until round 385 fixed campaign._dump_json's shared temp name; promoted so the fix cannot silently regress

test_swe_proc.py.why: process helpers; reads the whence corpus (15k reads) but does almost no interpreting

test_swe_scoreaudit.py.why: pure arithmetic over recorded campaign data, no interpreter reads at all

test_swe_triage.py.why: mutation triage over JSON; no interpreter reads at all

test_swe_depthceiling.py.why: round 389's ceiling tests: they pin the FRAME_SLACK derivation, the undercharge detection band and render's pair-coverage line, all of which go red on a language-constant change (FAST_MAX_DEPTH, MAX_NESTING, DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH) -- exactly the class round 383 found hiding in the slow tier for 15 rounds
